- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–7 days.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to drop; if below, tends to rise — adjust for 1–2% lagged momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to err on the side of overconfidence; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid overestimation.
